why: ONE EXHIBIT, ONE RUN — this row becomes it, and its title loses a word the museum has never printed. We held FIVE published rows for one special exhibit at the Minnesota Children's Museum, the largest single duplication on the calendar; this is the only one whose start DAY is the run's real first day, so it takes the span and the other four come down. THE NAME: the museum's own press release is headed '"Monsters on Vacation" Opens May 23 at Minnesota Children's Museum' and its Visitor Information line reads '"Monsters on Vacation" is open for play at Minnesota Children's Museum from May 23 through Jan. 10, 2027.' A second mcm.org page, /special-exhibit-gallery/, names the current special exhibit 'Monsters on Vacation' and nothing else, and /exhibits/ and /upcoming-special-exhibits/ never use 'Summer' either - the latter lists only 'The Questioneers: Read. Question. Think. PLAY!' (Jan. 23 - May 9, 2027) and 'Camp Hooray: An Exhibit Where Oops is Awesome' (Summer 2027). BUT 'Monsters on Summer Vacation' IS A REAL MUSEUM TITLE, which is why this row had it: mcm.org/monsters-are-taking-over-the-museum-this-summer/ is still live and reads 'Monsters on Summer Vacation opens June 8, 2024 and runs through Labor Day', describing an earlier run with a near-identical component list. So the stored title is not invented, it is two years stale - the wrong-year shape this project keeps finding, except that this time the wrong year is published on the organiser's own domain and anything reading mcm.org for this exhibit can land on it. The 2024 page is a standing trap, not a one-off. '(Special Exhibit)' goes with it: canonicalizeTitle deletes parenthetical contents, so dropping it is identity-neutral, and the exhibit's name is simply the name. THE DATES ARE NOT CHANGED, only the column they live in: the row already carried 2026-05-23 and 2027-01-10, which is the window the Visitor Information line prints. ONE HONEST GAP IN THAT, found by trying to refute it: no mcm.org page prints a year beside 'May 23'. Only the close carries one, 'Jan. 10, 2027'. The 2026 start year rests on three things instead - the museum's own post date of 8 May 2026 on /author/dcasper/, the 2027 close, and /upcoming-special-exhibits/ placing the successor exhibit at 'Jan. 23 - May 9, 2027', which only works if this one is running now. That is inference, not attestation, and it is recorded here rather than smoothed over; the start day is left exactly as the row already had it, so this correction asserts no year the pipeline did not already assert. The 17:00 stored on 2027-01-10 is a two-hour-style default and not a closing instant the museum publishes for this exhibit - neither page prints hours - so it is cleared and the run moves to multi_day_end, the column counted in days. ONE CONTRADICTION ON THE EVIDENCE PAGE, named rather than hidden: the intro sentence reads 'opens June 23', against 'May 23' in the headline, in the Visitor Information line and in the page's own URL slug. Three to one, and the June sentence sits beside 'Beginning in early June' and 'a Monster Party on June 6' - monster-themed events held while the exhibit is open. May 23 stands; the row already had it. RENDER IS UNCHANGED by the reshape: a 232-day span is far past EXPAND_MAX_DAYS either way, so daysSpanned returns 2026-05-23 alone under both shapes and isUpcoming was already false before this edit. The exhibit shows on /ongoing and on /this-weekend, which read the true uncapped span. Citation moves off womenspress.com/organizer/, a third-party organiser listing, onto the museum's own release. NOT STAMPED: the 09:00 start is printed on no mcm.org page read here, and both title and end_local are verify-relevant, so the row goes back through the verify pass to establish the hours - the right outcome for a listing whose name was wrong.
title: Monsters on Vacation

why: Duplicate chunk of the one 2026-05-23 to 2027-01-10 Monsters on Vacation run, now carried by e80b7021. Archive rather than draft because 17 August 2026 is a day the exhibit was genuinely open - the museum's release prints the run as 'from May 23 through Jan. 10, 2027' and 17 August falls inside it - so the archived page goes on saying a true thing. What is wrong is the shape around that start: a 147-day span whose first day is three months after the exhibit opened, presenting the middle of a run as its beginning. It was the second Monsters card on /ongoing and on /this-weekend for every weekend from 17 August. Citation is a third-party monthly guide (stpaulpublishing.com sample guide), not the museum.

Duplicate chunk of the one 2026-05-23 to 2027-01-10 Monsters on Vacation run, now carried by e80b7021, and the clearest proof of the mechanism: it is byte-identical to 9750dfbd in title, venue, city, end and citation, and differs only in starting 24 August instead of 17 August - one week later, because event_key is sha256(title | venue | start DAY) and the weekly pipeline writes the day it FOUND the exhibit. Archive rather than draft: 24 August 2026 is inside the printed run, so the archived page stays true.

Duplicate chunk of the one 2026-05-23 to 2027-01-10 Monsters on Vacation run, now carried by e80b7021. Archive rather than draft: 2 November 2026 is inside the printed run. Its end is right and its start is not - the museum prints one continuous window 'from May 23 through Jan. 10, 2027', not a run beginning in November. Citation is msp.kidsoutandabout.com, a third-party directory.

The fifth published row for one exhibit, and the only one that contradicts the museum on the closing date. It claims 12 November to 11 December 2026; the museum's own release - which THIS ROW CITES - prints 'from May 23 through Jan. 10, 2027'. The 11 December end is a 30-day default measured from the day the pipeline found the exhibit, and it was stamped verified on 2026-10-12 against the page that disagrees with it, which is the verify-pass weakness addressed in 219c6b4. Archived rather than hidden: 12 November 2026 is a day the exhibit is genuinely open and 11 December is inside the run, so the archived page asserts a true sub-window rather than an event that never happened - the line the 28 October re-dated-sessions incident drew. The run is carried by e80b7021 with the printed window. Not kept as the survivor despite having the best citation: its start is six months after the exhibit opened, and one production gets the row whose first day is the run's first day.

ONE SHOW, ONE RUN, AND NO 'OPENING' EVENT — this row becomes the Fall Flower Show's second display and loses a word Como does not publish. We held five published rows for it. Three pages on comozooconservatory.org carry the window and agree date for date: /como/sunken-garden-2/ prints 'Fall Flower Show 2026' as 'September 18 through October 18 and October 23 through November 29, 2026' with the year adjacent, and adds 'Sunken Garden will be closed for the mid-show change October 19 - October 22', which is what separates the two halves; /mmc-sunken-garden-live/ is headed 'The Fall Flower Show Is Now Open!' and prints the date line 'October 23 through November 29, 2026' on its own. So the second display runs 23 October to 29 November 2026, and this row's 18 November end is wrong by eleven days - a 27-day default from the day it was found, not a date either page prints. THE TITLE: Como publishes no Fall Flower Show 'Opening'. Measured on Como's own site rather than assumed: its event calendar carries NO fall flower show event of any kind for 2026, the site's event search for 'flower show' answers 'There were no results found', and the day view for 23 October 2026 - the display's own first day - lists eight routine programs (Polar Bear Program, Zookeeper Talk, Sparky and Friends twice, Story Time, Gardener Chat, Gorilla Program, Fish Chat) and no flower show. The event sitemap does hold opening-day URLs, but for the holiday, summer and spring shows and for no fall show in any year; the only /event/fall-flower-show/ URL is a passed 2020 'Visit Virtually!' listing. So the pattern exists at Como and was never applied to the fall show. This row is the whole second display, so 'Opening' is deleted. 'Part 2' goes too: the sunken-garden page labels the halves Part 1 and Part 2 but prints no date line for either, while the currently-live page calls the 23 October to 29 November window simply 'The Fall Flower Show' - and Part 1 ended on 18 October and is archived, so a part number now tells a reader nothing. The 16:00 end on 29 November is cleared rather than moved: neither page prints the conservatory's hours, so it is an unattested closing instant, and the run goes to multi_day_end, the column counted in days. The 10:00 start is left exactly as it was - also unattested, but this correction is not the place to invent it. RENDER: at 38 days the run is past EXPAND_MAX_DAYS=14 under both the old shape and the new, so daysSpanned returns 2026-10-23 alone either way and isUpcoming was already false; the show is carried by /ongoing and by /this-weekend, which read the true uncapped span. Citation already points at /como/sunken-garden-2/ and is left alone, so source_checked_at keeps its place in the queue. TWO WRONG-YEAR TRAPS ON COMO'S OWN DOMAIN, named so the next pass does not step in them: /mums-the-word-at-como/ puts the second half at 5 to 27 November behind a closure of 'October 31 - November 4', and /fall-flower-show-flamingos/ says 'Part II of the Fall Flower Show is now open through November 28th' with no year beside it. The first is a 2022 post and the second a 2021 post, and both are the same October-into-November shape as the real 2026 window. Only the pages that print '2026' adjacent were used. NOT STAMPED: the 2026-10-22 stamp clears because title and end_local are both verify-relevant, and it should - it rested partly on the 18 November end the organiser contradicts.
title: Fall Flower Show

why: Duplicate of the one 23 October to 29 November 2026 Fall Flower Show second display, now carried by 7d5fa345. Archive rather than draft because 26 October 2026 is a day the show was genuinely open - Como prints 'October 23 through November 29, 2026' - so the archived page stays true. Its 25 November end is a 31-day default from the day it was found, four days short of the printed close, and its start is three days after the display opened. Same title as the survivor before the rename, same venue, same citation; it keyed apart only because the pipeline wrote the day it found the show.

Duplicate of the one 23 October to 29 November 2026 Fall Flower Show second display, now carried by 7d5fa345. Archive rather than draft: 1 November 2026 is inside the printed window. Its 1 to 16 November range appears on neither Como page read here - /como/sunken-garden-2/ prints 'October 23 through November 29, 2026' and /mmc-sunken-garden-live/ the same - and it was stamped verified on 2026-10-18 anyway. The 'Lion-Inspired' theme comes from comofriends.org/category/events/, a category listing on the fundraising partner's site rather than the conservatory's own show page; the conservatory describes Part 2 as bright yellow, dark red, green and white chrysanthemums and names no lion, so the theme is dropped with the row rather than carried onto the survivor.

Duplicate of the one 23 October to 29 November 2026 Fall Flower Show second display, now carried by 7d5fa345, and the one that was actually being seen: at 13 days its span is INSIDE EXPAND_MAX_DAYS=14, so unlike the other four it expanded across day pages and was the only Fall Flower card on /day from 1 to 13 November. That is also what makes it the worst of them - a capped-looking 13-day run asserting that the show closes on 13 November, which is sixteen days before the date Como prints twice. Rule 5, true spans and never capped expansions. Archive rather than draft because 1 November 2026 is a day the show was genuinely open, so the archived page asserts a true sub-window. Archiving it does cost reach: the survivor is a 38-day run and therefore past the cap, so no Fall Flower card appears on a day page after this - the isUpcoming over-cap defect, which is a code fix and not a correction.

Duplicate of the one 23 October to 29 November 2026 Fall Flower Show second display, now carried by 7d5fa345. Archive rather than draft: 2 November 2026 is inside the printed window. This is the row that had the END right - 29 November, from the conservatory's own currently-live page - and the start wrong by ten days, which is why the survivor takes its date and not its row: identity is the start DAY, and 23 October is the day the display opened.
